series.title: Annotation quality control and biological assays

lessons.title: PyPI, GitHub, and conda-forge
lessons.description: Choose the official source for a packaged release, desktop installer, development branch, or future conda-forge package.
objectives: Identify the official PyPI package and GitHub repository.
Distinguish stable releases from the nightly branch.
Understand the current conda-forge publication status.
lessons.prerequisite: No installation is required.

scenes.narration: Before installing spaCR, choose the official source. PyPI provides the released Python package, GitHub provides source code and desktop installers, and conda-forge will become an option once its package is published.
scenes.speech_text: Before installing spacer, choose the official source. pie-P-I provides the released Python package, [GitHub](/ɡˈɪthˌʌb/) provides source code and desktop installers, and [conda-forge](/kˈɑndə fˌɔɹʤ/) will become an option once its package is published.

scenes.narration: On PyPI, the release header shows the current stable version and the pip install spacr command.
scenes.speech_text: On pie-P-I, the release header shows the current stable version and the pip install spacer command.

scenes.narration: The Project links section opens the documentation, homepage, issue tracker, and source repository.
scenes.speech_text: The Project links section opens the documentation, homepage, issue tracker, and source repository.

scenes.narration: On GitHub, use the branch selector to choose the source line. Main is the released line; nightly contains newer work still being tested.
scenes.speech_text: On [GitHub](/ɡˈɪthˌʌb/), use the branch selector to choose the source line. Main is the released line; nightly contains newer work still being tested.

scenes.narration: In a GitHub Release, expand Assets to download the Windows, macOS, or Linux installer, the Python package files, or the checksum list.
scenes.speech_text: In a [GitHub](/ɡˈɪthˌʌb/) Release, expand Assets to download the Windows, [macOS](/mˈækOˌɛs/), or Linux installer, the Python package files, or the checksum list.

scenes.narration: Conda-forge does not publish spaCR yet. Today, create a Conda environment and install spaCR from PyPI; use the conda-forge channel only after the package is published.
scenes.speech_text: [Conda-forge](/kˈɑndə fˌɔɹʤ/) does not publish spacer yet. Today, create a [Conda](/kˈɑndə/) environment and install spacer from pie-P-I; use the [conda-forge](/kˈɑndə fˌɔɹʤ/) channel only after the package is published.

scenes.narration: Use PyPI or pip for a Python environment, GitHub Releases for a desktop installer, and nightly only when you need unreleased work. Next, choose the installation tutorial for your route.
scenes.speech_text: Use pie-P-I or pip for a Python environment, [GitHub](/ɡˈɪthˌʌb/) Releases for a desktop installer, and nightly only when you need unreleased work. Next, choose the installation tutorial for your route.

lessons.title: Installation with Conda
lessons.description: Create an isolated Python 3.12 environment and install the desktop or headless package into it.
objectives: Create and verify an isolated spaCR environment.
Choose the desktop or headless installation.
Validate the installation before launching spaCR.
lessons.prerequisite: Install Miniforge, Miniconda, Anaconda, or another Conda-compatible manager.

scenes.narration: Use a Conda environment to isolate spaCR and its scientific dependencies. Python three point twelve is the example because it currently supports the widest range of optional packages.
scenes.speech_text: Use a [Conda](/kˈɑndə/) environment to isolate spacer and its scientific dependencies. Python three point twelve is the example because it currently supports the widest range of optional packages.

scenes.narration: Open a Conda-enabled terminal and create an environment named spacr with Python three point twelve and pip.
scenes.speech_text: Open a [Conda](/kˈɑndə/)-enabled terminal and create an environment named spacer with Python three point twelve and pip.

scenes.narration: Activate the environment. Confirm that Python belongs to the spacr environment before installing anything.
scenes.speech_text: Activate the environment. Confirm that Python belongs to the spacer environment before installing anything.

scenes.narration: Upgrade pip through the active Python interpreter. Using python -m pip prevents a different pip executable from receiving the package.
scenes.speech_text: Upgrade pip through the active Python interpreter. Using python dash m pip prevents a different pip executable from receiving the package.

scenes.narration: For the desktop application, install spacr with the qt extra. Use the plain spacr package for a headless workstation or server.
scenes.speech_text: For the desktop application, install spacer with the cute extra. Use the plain spacer package for a headless workstation or server.

scenes.narration: Run spacr-doctor before the first launch. It reports the active installation, Qt, PyTorch, optional components, and hardware support with a suggested fix for every failed check.
scenes.speech_text: Run spacer doctor before the first launch. It reports the active installation, cute, [PyTorch](/pˈItˌɔɹʧ/), optional components, and hardware support with a suggested fix for every failed check.

scenes.narration: After spacr-doctor passes, keep this environment activated whenever you run spaCR.
scenes.speech_text: After spacer doctor passes, keep this environment activated whenever you run spacer.

lessons.title: Installation with pip
lessons.description: Install spaCR into a standard virtual environment without using Conda.
objectives: Create a virtual environment on each supported operating system.
Install the correct spaCR package variant.
Verify the environment before launching the application.
lessons.prerequisite: Install a supported Python version; Python 3.12 is recommended.

scenes.narration: The pip route works on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Always use an isolated virtual environment rather than modifying the operating system's Python installation.
scenes.speech_text: The pip route works on Windows, [macOS](/mˈækOˌɛs/), and Linux. Always use an isolated virtual environment rather than modifying the operating system's Python installation.

scenes.narration: On macOS or Linux, create the environment with Python three point twelve, then activate it from its bin directory.
scenes.speech_text: On [macOS](/mˈækOˌɛs/) or Linux, create the environment with Python three point twelve, then activate it from its bin directory.

scenes.narration: On Windows, use the Python launcher to create the environment and activate it from the Scripts directory.
scenes.speech_text: On Windows, use the Python launcher to create the environment and activate it from the Scripts directory.

scenes.narration: Upgrade pip in the active environment. The command python -m pip keeps installation tied to the Python you just activated.
scenes.speech_text: Upgrade pip in the active environment. The command python dash m pip keeps installation tied to the Python you just activated.

scenes.narration: Install the plain spacr package for headless use, or spacr with the qt extra for the desktop interface.
scenes.speech_text: Install the plain spacer package for headless use, or spacer with the cute extra for the desktop interface.

scenes.narration: Verify the imported version and run spacr-doctor. Resolve any failed checks before opening experimental data.
scenes.speech_text: Verify the imported version and run spacer doctor. Resolve any failed checks before opening experimental data.

scenes.narration: The environment is now ready. Keep it activated whenever you use spaCR, and use python -m pip install --upgrade spacr when you intentionally update it.
scenes.speech_text: The environment is now ready. Keep it activated whenever you use spacer, and use python dash m pip install dash dash upgrade spacer when you intentionally update it.

lessons.title: Platform installers
lessons.description: Install spaCR on Windows, macOS, or Linux without an existing Python or Conda installation.
objectives: Select the correct installer for Windows, macOS, or Linux.
Handle platform security and acceleration choices.
Locate diagnostics if installation fails.
lessons.prerequisite: Download the installer for your operating system from the official GitHub release.

scenes.narration: The lightweight native installers create a private Python three point twelve runtime, then download Qt, PyTorch, spaCR, and its scientific dependencies.
scenes.speech_text: The lightweight native installers create a private Python three point twelve runtime, then download cute, [PyTorch](/pˈItˌɔɹʧ/), spacer, and its scientific dependencies.

scenes.narration: Download installers only from the latest spaCR GitHub Release. Match the file to your operating system and use the published SHA-256 file when you need to verify the download.
scenes.speech_text: Download installers only from the latest spacer [GitHub](/ɡˈɪthˌʌb/) Release. Match the file to your operating system and use the published S H A two fifty six file when you need to verify the download.

scenes.narration: On Windows ten or eleven, open the online setup executable. The portable CPU installation is the default; NVIDIA acceleration is an optional installer component.
scenes.speech_text: On Windows ten or eleven, open the online setup executable. The portable CPU installation is the default; NVIDIA acceleration is an optional installer component.

scenes.narration: On macOS eleven or newer, open the universal package for Intel and Apple silicon. If Gatekeeper blocks the unnotarized package, use Privacy and Security, Open Anyway, then run it again.
scenes.speech_text: On [macOS](/mˈækOˌɛs/) eleven or newer, open the universal package for Intel and Apple silicon. If Gatekeeper blocks the [unnotarized](/ʌnnˈOTəɹIzd/) package, use Privacy and Security, Open Anyway, then run it again.

scenes.narration: On sixty four bit Linux, make the downloaded .run file executable, then start it from a terminal. The default installation uses CPU-compatible PyTorch.
scenes.speech_text: On sixty four bit Linux, make the downloaded .run file executable, then start it from a terminal. The default installation uses CPU compatible [PyTorch](/pˈItˌɔɹʧ/).

scenes.narration: For supported NVIDIA hardware on Linux, pass --torch-backend auto. This selects acceleration when available without making CUDA libraries the silent default.
scenes.speech_text: For supported NVIDIA hardware on Linux, pass dash dash torch back end auto. This selects acceleration when available without making [CUDA](/kˈuːdᵊ/) libraries the silent default.

scenes.narration: Each installer validates the replacement before switching versions. An interrupted update leaves the previous environment intact, and install.log remains in the private spaCR installation directory.
scenes.speech_text: Each installer validates the replacement before switching versions. An interrupted update leaves the previous environment intact, and install dot log remains in the private spacer installation directory.

scenes.narration: After installation, use the operating system launcher. No separate Python or Conda setup is required.
scenes.speech_text: After installation, use the operating system launcher. No separate Python or [Conda](/kˈɑndə/) setup is required.

lessons.title: Home screen and navigation
lessons.description: Find modules, inspect application status, and move into a workflow from the spaCR Home screen.
objectives: Find modules from Home, category tabs, or the sidebar.
Read system and module-state information.
Open a workflow and confirm the active module.
lessons.prerequisite: Install and launch the spaCR desktop application.

scenes.narration: Home groups spaCR modules by workflow so you can move from image processing through analysis and quality control.
scenes.speech_text: Home groups spacer modules by workflow so you can move from image processing through analysis and quality control.

scenes.narration: Use the left sidebar to switch sections. Choose Home whenever you want to return to the complete module library.
scenes.speech_text: Use the left sidebar to switch sections. Choose Home whenever you want to return to the complete module library.

scenes.narration: Browse the category tabs and workflow rows to find a module. Each tile opens one workflow, and its color indicates whether the module is alpha, beta, or stable.
scenes.speech_text: Browse the category tabs and workflow rows to find a module. Each tile opens one workflow, and its color indicates whether the module is alpha, beta, or stable.

scenes.narration: The right panel shows current system use, release news, and the module-state legend. Check system use before starting expensive work.
scenes.speech_text: The right panel shows current system use, release news, and the module-state legend. Check system use before starting expensive work.

scenes.narration: Select a module tile to open its settings screen. The module name and description at the top confirm which workflow is active.
scenes.speech_text: Select a module tile to open its settings screen. The module name and description at the top confirm which workflow is active.

lessons.title: Python API and headless workflows
lessons.description: Run reproducible spaCR pipelines from Python or a shell without the desktop interface.
objectives: Confirm that spaCR is available from Python.
Choose and configure a spacr-run pipeline.
Validate a small test before a full headless run.
lessons.prerequisite: Complete one installation tutorial first.

scenes.narration: Import spaCR and print its version to confirm that the active Python environment can use the package.
scenes.speech_text: Import spacer and print its version to confirm that the active Python environment can use the package.

scenes.narration: Run spacr-run with the list option to see the available pipeline entry points, including mask, measure, annotate, classify, and report.
scenes.speech_text: Run spacer run with the list option to see the available pipeline entry points, including mask, measure, annotate, [classify](/klˈæsəfI/), and report.

scenes.narration: Start a module with spacr-run, the module name, and an exported settings file. spaCR validates paths, channels, workers, and hardware options before work begins.
scenes.speech_text: Start a module with spacer run, the module name, and an exported settings file. spacer validates paths, channels, workers, and hardware options before work begins.

scenes.narration: Add the test option to process a small representative subset first. Review the preview and saved log before submitting a full unattended run.
scenes.speech_text: Add the test option to process a small representative subset first. Review the preview and saved log before submitting a full unattended run.

scenes.narration: Remove the test option for the full run. Headless jobs save the same outputs, settings, version record, and logs as the desktop workflow.
scenes.speech_text: Remove the test option for the full run. Headless jobs save the same outputs, settings, version record, and logs as the desktop workflow.

lessons.title: Mask
lessons.description: Configure segmentation, validate it with Live Preview, and create masks for downstream measurement.
objectives: Verify source metadata and channel mapping.
Configure only the segmentation controls required by the images.
Use Live Preview to validate masks before a full run.
lessons.prerequisite: Use a microscopy source whose channel identities and filename metadata are known.

scenes.narration: Mask places settings on the left and the runtime console on the right. The console reports validation, progress, warnings, and saved outputs.
scenes.speech_text: Mask places settings on the left and the runtime console on the right. The console reports validation, progress, warnings, and saved outputs.

scenes.narration: Drop the source image folder into Mask. Confirm the detected filename pattern and metadata, then map each acquisition channel to its biological signal. In this example, the four channels contain nuclei, endoplasmic reticulum, lipid droplets, and parasites.
scenes.speech_text: Drop the source image folder into Mask. Confirm the detected filename pattern and metadata, then map each acquisition channel to its biological signal. In this example, the four channels contain nuclei, [endoplasmic](/ˌɛndOplˈæzmɪk/) reticulum, lipid droplets, and parasites.

scenes.narration: Essentials shows the controls needed for a typical run. Use All only when you need advanced options, Modified to review changed values, and Recipes to save a configuration you will reuse.
scenes.speech_text: Essentials shows the controls needed for a typical run. Use All only when you need advanced options, Modified to review changed values, and Recipes to save a configuration you will reuse.

scenes.narration: In Input and Metadata, verify the source folder, channel assignments, magnification, and filename metadata before configuring segmentation.
scenes.speech_text: In Input and Metadata, verify the source folder, channel assignments, magnification, and filename metadata before configuring segmentation.

scenes.narration: Workflow and Test Run controls which masks are created, whether existing work resumes, and how many representative fields are used for a test.
scenes.speech_text: Workflow and Test Run controls which masks are created, whether existing work resumes, and how many representative fields are used for a test.

scenes.narration: The cell, nucleus, pathogen, and organelle sections each group the model, channel, core thresholds, and object filters for that compartment. Change only settings needed for the current images.
scenes.speech_text: The cell, nucleus, pathogen, and organelle sections each group the model, channel, core thresholds, and object filters for that compartment. Change only settings needed for the current images.

scenes.narration: Enable Live Preview, load a representative field, and choose the object you are tuning. This example previews the cell signal.
scenes.speech_text: Enable Live Preview, load a representative field, and choose the object you are tuning. This example previews the cell signal.

scenes.narration: In Live settings, confirm the object and channel first. Adjust diameter, flow threshold, or cell probability only when the preview gives you a reason.
scenes.speech_text: In Live settings, confirm the object and channel first. Adjust diameter, flow threshold, or cell probability only when the preview gives you a reason.

scenes.narration: Turn on Propagate settings so the values you validate here become the settings used by the full run.
scenes.speech_text: Turn on Propagate settings so the values you validate here become the settings used by the full run.

scenes.narration: Run the preview and inspect Overlay beside the source. Boundaries should follow the visible cells without joining neighbors or missing clear objects.
scenes.speech_text: Run the preview and inspect Overlay beside the source. Boundaries should follow the visible cells without joining neighbors or missing clear objects.

scenes.narration: Switch to Flows to inspect the direction field used by Cellpose. Irregular flow patterns can help explain masks that split or merge incorrectly.
scenes.speech_text: Switch to Flows to inspect the direction field used by [Cellpose](/sˈɛlpˌOz/). Irregular flow patterns can help explain masks that split or merge incorrectly.

scenes.narration: Masks isolates the final labels against a black background. Use it to check object coverage and separation without the source image underneath.
scenes.speech_text: Masks isolates the final labels against a black background. Use it to check object coverage and separation without the source image underneath.

scenes.narration: Object filters update the cached preview immediately. Raise minimum area only enough to remove obvious fragments; the correct cutoff depends on image scale.
scenes.speech_text: Object filters update the cached preview immediately. Raise minimum area only enough to remove obvious fragments; the correct cutoff depends on image scale.

scenes.narration: Compare the filtered overlay with the original preview. Genuine cells should remain; if they disappear, lower the minimum area.
scenes.speech_text: Compare the filtered overlay with the original preview. Genuine cells should remain; if they disappear, lower the minimum area.

scenes.narration: Choose the masks and intermediate files you need in Output and Storage. Run a small test first, then process the full source after the preview and console checks pass.
scenes.speech_text: Choose the masks and intermediate files you need in Output and Storage. Run a small test first, then process the full source after the preview and console checks pass.

lessons.title: Measure
lessons.description: Extract object-level features from images and masks, then inspect the resulting crop gallery and database output.
objectives: Verify image channels and mask-plane mapping.
Choose only the feature families, filters, and crops the analysis needs.
Validate a test in Live Preview before writing full measurement outputs.
lessons.prerequisite: Complete Mask and confirm that the merged project contains usable image and label planes.

scenes.narration: Measure places settings on the left and the runtime console on the right. The console reports source validation, progress, warnings, and saved measurement output.
scenes.speech_text: Measure places settings on the left and the runtime console on the right. The console reports source validation, progress, warnings, and saved measurement output.

scenes.narration: Choose the merged project folder produced by Mask. Measure reads the stored image, mask, and project metadata directly.
scenes.speech_text: Choose the merged project folder produced by Mask. Measure reads the stored image, mask, and project metadata directly.

scenes.narration: Start with Essentials. Use All for advanced controls, Modified to audit changed values, and Recipes when the same measurement setup will be reused.
scenes.speech_text: Start with Essentials. Use All for advanced controls, Modified to audit changed values, and Recipes when the same measurement setup will be reused.

scenes.narration: In Mask and Channel Mapping, verify the image channels and the label planes for cells, nuclei, pathogens, organelles, and any derived compartments.
scenes.speech_text: In Mask and Channel Mapping, verify the image channels and the label planes for cells, nuclei, pathogens, organelles, and any derived compartments.

scenes.narration: Measurement Features selects the intensity, morphology, texture, colocalization, and spatial summaries needed for the analysis. Leave unused feature families off.
scenes.speech_text: Measurement Features selects the intensity, morphology, texture, co-localization, and spatial summaries needed for the analysis. Leave unused feature families off.

scenes.narration: Object Filtering removes known artifacts, while Crop Output controls whether representative object images are saved for annotation or classification. Choose filters and crop scale from the experiment rather than copying fixed values.
scenes.speech_text: Object Filtering removes known artifacts, while Crop Output controls whether representative object images are saved for annotation or classification. Choose filters and crop scale from the experiment rather than copying fixed values.

scenes.narration: Preview and Diagnostics defines a small test sample. Use it before measuring the full experiment.
scenes.speech_text: Preview and Diagnostics defines a small test sample. Use it before measuring the full experiment.

scenes.narration: Enable Live Preview and load a completed merged array. The gallery groups real object crops so you can check mask assignments, channel content, and crop framing.
scenes.speech_text: Enable Live Preview and load a completed merged array. The gallery groups real object crops so you can check mask assignments, channel content, and crop framing.

scenes.narration: Switch gallery channels to inspect each biological signal. This display choice helps quality control and does not limit which configured channels are measured.
scenes.speech_text: Switch gallery channels to inspect each biological signal. This display choice helps quality control and does not limit which configured channels are measured.

scenes.narration: After the test succeeds, run the full source. Measure saves traceable object rows in measurements dot db and any requested crops beside the project outputs.
scenes.speech_text: After the test succeeds, run the full source. Measure saves traceable object rows in measurements dot D B and any requested crops beside the project outputs.

lessons.title: Annotate
lessons.description: Review object crops, assign consistent labels, audit coverage, and hand saved labels to a classifier.
objectives: Configure a consistent crop view and annotation column.
Label, navigate, undo, and save efficiently.
Audit coverage before handing labels to a classifier.
lessons.prerequisite: Complete Measure with object crops and decide on a documented class scheme.

scenes.narration: Annotate prioritizes the crop grid. Open the console only when you need database messages, save status, warnings, or local help, then hide it to return space to the images.
scenes.speech_text: Annotate prioritizes the crop grid. Open the console only when you need database messages, save status, warnings, or local help, then hide it to return space to the images.

scenes.narration: Open a measured project, choose or create an annotation column, and confirm that the expected object crops load. Define what each class means before labeling begins.
scenes.speech_text: Open a measured project, choose or create an annotation column, and confirm that the expected object crops load. Define what each class means before labeling begins.

scenes.narration: Settings controls the displayed channels, crop appearance, object filters, and optional uncertainty queue. Keep the view consistent for everyone contributing labels.
scenes.speech_text: Settings controls the displayed channels, crop appearance, object filters, and optional uncertainty queue. Keep the view consistent for everyone contributing labels.

scenes.narration: Open the keyboard reference for the small set of actions used repeatedly: assign a class, move focus, skip, undo, and save or advance.
scenes.speech_text: Open the keyboard reference for the small set of actions used repeatedly: assign a class, move focus, skip, undo, and save or advance.

scenes.narration: Assign labels with number keys or the mouse. The class-colored ring confirms the saved label, and focus advances so many objects can be reviewed efficiently.
scenes.speech_text: Assign labels with number keys or the mouse. The class-colored ring confirms the saved label, and focus advances so many objects can be reviewed efficiently.

scenes.narration: Use navigation and undo to correct a recent choice without clearing other saved work. Save before moving to another page or ending the session.
scenes.speech_text: Use navigation and undo to correct a recent choice without clearing other saved work. Save before moving to another page or ending the session.

scenes.narration: Coverage shows whether labels span classes, plates, wells, sources, and active-learning rounds. Add examples from missing groups before training.
scenes.speech_text: Coverage shows whether labels span classes, plates, wells, sources, and active-learning rounds. Add examples from missing groups before training.

scenes.narration: When enough representative labels exist, Retrain can score the remaining crops and prioritize uncertain examples. Treat this as an optional review aid, not a replacement for coverage.
scenes.speech_text: When enough representative labels exist, Retrain can score the remaining crops and prioritize uncertain examples. Treat this as an optional review aid, not a replacement for coverage.

scenes.narration: Train CV sends image crops and this annotation column to the vision classifier. Train XG sends the same labels to the feature-based classifier; both open a configured module without starting training automatically.
scenes.speech_text: Train CV sends image crops and this annotation column to the vision [classifier](/klˈæsəfIəɹ/). Train XG sends the same labels to the feature-based [classifier](/klˈæsəfIəɹ/); both open a configured module without starting training automatically.

scenes.narration: Annotations remain in measurements dot db with object identifiers and provenance intact. Continue until coverage is adequate for the intended model or quality-control decision.
scenes.speech_text: Annotations remain in measurements dot D B with object identifiers and provenance intact. Continue until coverage is adequate for the intended model or quality-control decision.

lessons.title: Classify, computer vision
lessons.description: Train and evaluate an image classifier from annotated object crops, with grouped validation and optional hyperparameter search.
objectives: Map saved labels and object crops into a leakage-safe dataset.
Configure a baseline model and grouped evaluation.
Use Hyperparameter Search only for a focused comparison.
lessons.prerequisite: Complete Annotate with documented classes and representative coverage across the intended plates or wells.

scenes.narration: Classify CV trains image models on annotated object crops. The console reports dataset checks, training progress, held-out metrics, inference, warnings, and output paths.
scenes.speech_text: [Classify](/klˈæsəfI/) CV trains image models on annotated object crops. The console reports dataset checks, training progress, held-out metrics, inference, warnings, and output paths.

scenes.narration: Plate Sources and Workflow selects the measured projects and the stages to run: build a split, train, evaluate, or apply an existing checkpoint.
scenes.speech_text: Plate Sources and Workflow selects the measured projects and the stages to run: build a split, train, evaluate, or apply an existing checkpoint.

scenes.narration: Start with Essentials, use Modified to audit deliberate changes, and open All only for controls required by the experiment. Save a Recipe when the setup will be repeated.
scenes.speech_text: Start with Essentials, use Modified to audit deliberate changes, and open All only for controls required by the experiment. Save a Recipe when the setup will be repeated.

scenes.narration: Labels and Classes selects the annotation or metadata field used as ground truth and maps its saved values to documented class names. Verify that mapping before training.
scenes.speech_text: Labels and Classes selects the annotation or metadata field used as ground truth and maps its saved values to documented class names. Verify that mapping before training.

scenes.narration: Crops and Dataset Split chooses the object images, channels, balancing, and held-out fraction. Group related images by plate or well so near-duplicates cannot leak between training and evaluation.
scenes.speech_text: Crops and Dataset Split chooses the object images, channels, balancing, and held-out fraction. Group related images by plate or well so near-duplicates cannot leak between training and evaluation.

scenes.narration: Model Architecture selects the network, input channels and size, pretrained weights, and normalization expected by the images. Begin with one reasonable baseline.
scenes.speech_text: Model Architecture selects the network, input channels and size, pre-trained weights, and normalization expected by the images. Begin with one reasonable baseline.

scenes.speech_text: Optimization and Loss contains learning rate, augmentation, batches, epochs, and early stopping. Change a small number of controls at a time and judge them on validation behavior.

scenes.speech_text: Evaluation Workbench adds grouped or nested evaluation, calibration, and strict identity and content-leakage checks. Keep the final held-out data separate from model selection.

scenes.narration: Full Dataset and Inference applies the chosen checkpoint, writes probabilities and class calls, and saves representative high-confidence examples for review.
scenes.speech_text: Full Dataset and Inference applies the chosen checkpoint, writes probabilities and class calls, and saves representative high-confidence examples for review.

scenes.narration: Enable Hyperparameter Search when several plausible configurations need comparison. The mini workbench runs grouped trials and displays each score, fold variation, parameters, and status.
scenes.speech_text: Enable hyper-parameter Search when several plausible configurations need comparison. The mini workbench runs grouped trials and displays each score, fold variation, parameters, and status.

scenes.narration: Search Settings defines a focused candidate space, ranking metric, grouped folds, and trial budget. Avoid broad searches that spend compute on choices the experiment cannot distinguish.
scenes.speech_text: Search Settings defines a focused candidate space, ranking metric, grouped folds, and trial budget. Avoid broad searches that spend compute on choices the experiment cannot distinguish.

scenes.narration: Run first validates labels and splits, then trains and evaluates the configured model. Review held-out metrics and examples before applying it broadly; spaCR stores the checkpoint, predictions, settings, and run record.
scenes.speech_text: Run first validates labels and splits, then trains and evaluates the configured model. Review held-out metrics and examples before applying it broadly; spacer stores the checkpoint, predictions, settings, and run record.

lessons.title: Classify, machine learning
lessons.description: Train and evaluate a feature-based classifier from measured objects, with plate-aware correction and optional hyperparameter search.
objectives: Prepare valid measurement features and plate-aware labels.
Configure grouped validation and interpretable outputs.
Use Hyperparameter Search for a focused, reproducible comparison.
lessons.prerequisite: Complete Measure and provide a reliable label or control mapping with leakage-safe grouping columns.

scenes.narration: Classify ML trains a classical model on per-object measurements. The console reports database loading, feature preparation, validation, importance, predictions, and errors.
scenes.speech_text: [Classify](/klˈæsəfI/) ML trains a classical model on per-object measurements. The console reports database loading, feature preparation, validation, importance, predictions, and errors.
